skill.name: fda-database
skill.description: Query openFDA data for drugs, devices, foods, veterinary products, recalls, adverse events, approvals, labels, and substance identifiers.
skill.summary: Access openFDA regulatory datasets with guided queries and reusable Python helpers.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: This skill provides openFDA query guidance and Python helpers for public FDA datasets. Static matches for network calls, API key handling, cache writes, and markdown backticks are consistent with the stated function. A low-severity semantic issue remains because SKILL.md includes a product-promotion instruction for K-Dense Web.

remediation.issue: Embedded product promotion guidance in SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Move K-Dense Web promotion to marketplace metadata or remove it from operational skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Optional FDA API key handling appears in scripts and examples.
remediation.suggestion: Document that FDA_API_KEY is optional, never log full request URLs, and keep keys out of examples.

remediation.issue: Response caching writes files to a local cache directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document the cache directory, TTL, and opt-out setting for users who do not want local cache files.

content.value_statement: FDA data is spread across many specialized endpoints. This skill guides safe openFDA queries for research, surveillance, and regulatory review.
actual_capabilities: Query openFDA drug adverse events, labels, NDC records, recalls, approvals, and shortages.
Search medical device events, 510(k) clearances, PMA approvals, classifications, recalls, and UDI records.
Analyze food recalls, food adverse events, dietary supplement reports, and allergen-related enforcement data.
Look up animal and veterinary adverse event records by species, breed, product, or reaction.
Retrieve substance data such as UNII identifiers, names, CAS mappings, and chemical properties.
Use included Python helpers for rate limiting, pagination, response caching, and common query patterns.
limitations: The skill depends on openFDA availability, schema coverage, and public dataset update schedules.
Results are regulatory data records, not medical advice or a substitute for clinical review.
Some workflows need an FDA API key to avoid daily request limits.
The helper scripts can create a local response cache when caching is enabled.

use_cases.title: Review Drug Safety Signals
use_cases.description: Summarize adverse event counts, common reactions, serious reports, labels, and recalls for a selected drug.

use_cases.title: Track Device Regulatory History
use_cases.description: Find device adverse events, clearances, classifications, PMA records, UDI data, and recall activity.

use_cases.title: Monitor Food Recall Risks
use_cases.description: Search food enforcement records by allergen, contamination term, classification, status, and recall date.

prompt_templates.title: Find Drug Label Information
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the FDA database skill to find label information for [drug]. Summarize indications, warnings, dosage fields, and the source endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Check Recent Recalls
prompt_templates.prompt: Search openFDA recalls for [product or ingredient]. Group results by classification, reason, status, and recall initiation date.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Safety Profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare adverse event profiles for [drug A], [drug B], and [drug C]. Include total reports, serious reports, and common reactions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Regulatory Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cross-database FDA review for [product]. Combine events, labels, approvals, recalls, identifiers, and data quality caveats.

output_examples.output: A concise safety profile with event volume, top reported reactions, serious event count, recent recalls, and endpoint notes.

output_examples.input: Monitor Class I food recalls for undeclared peanut.
output_examples.output: A grouped recall summary showing affected products, recall reasons, dates, firm names, statuses, and public data limitations.

output_examples.input: Compare pacemaker adverse events and recalls.
output_examples.output: A device surveillance summary with event types, recent reports, recall records, classification context, and recommended follow-up queries.

best_practices: Use precise field searches before broad wildcard searches.
Set FDA_API_KEY for higher limits when running repeated analyses.
Document endpoint names, query terms, dates, and known missing fields in every result summary.
anti_patterns: Do not treat adverse event counts as incidence rates without denominator data.
Do not make clinical or legal conclusions from openFDA records alone.
Do not run broad paginated searches without rate limits, caps, and a clear purpose.

faq.question: Does this skill require an FDA API key?
faq.answer: No. A key is optional, but it raises daily request limits for heavier research workflows.

faq.question: Can it query drug and device data?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers drug, device, food, animal, veterinary, and substance endpoints from openFDA.

faq.question: Does it provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It helps retrieve and summarize public regulatory records for qualified review.

faq.question: Can it cache results locally?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper can write response cache files to reduce repeated API calls.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What are common data caveats?
faq.answer: Reports may be incomplete, duplicated, delayed, or missing fields depending on the source endpoint.
